reconcile.connective: Defenders read the daily bullock as the seven-day consecration rite, while the two lambs alone are the perpetual daily tamid the Numbers law repeats.

discrepancy.connective: Steven DiMattei argues that Numbers 28 claims the daily tamid was instituted at Sinai while Leviticus records no such offering, so Exodus 29:38-42 was a later Priestly insertion written to buttress that claim.

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, Contradictions in the Bible (contradictionsinthebible.com, 2014)

excerpts.excerpt_text: That is, every day of the seven days of consecration …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill explicitly limits the daily bullock of Exo 29:36 to the seven days of priestly consecration, which is precisely why it is absent from the perpetual daily tamid of Num 28 — the core harmonization of this row.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Exodus 29:36
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, restricting the daily bullock to the seven days of consecration so that the perpetual daily order is the two lambs of Num 28.
